Sol.role: Where every chain starts. The capitalist trunks head into Leo–Virgo; France and China run their own trees in other directions. First gate-layer departs ~2117, the year the wormhole breakthrough is cracked.

Wolf 359.role: The first waystation and the timeline's anchor (gate operational 2132). A dim flare star — a shared stepping-stone the US trunk and British spur both ride toward the Virgo cluster.

Ross 128.role: A quiet M-dwarf relay. Short, comfortable hops in and out — the easy middle of the shared corridor.

FL Virginis.role: A red-dwarf binary. Before GL Virginis was inserted, the next jump was a brutal ~12.5 ly; splitting it tamed the corridor's worst stretch.

GL Virginis.role: Where the corridor forks. The US trunk continues to Gliese 1154; the Commonwealth spur peels off here via Gliese 486. This node stays lit as long as either bloc is active — Britain's road home runs through it.

Gliese 1154.role: The last relay before Sonora, and a second branch point (→ 61 Virginis). The Magellan fleet breeds its embryos here and sprints the final 9.9 ly to Beta Virginis at 0.8c so the seeds survive.

Beta Virginis.role: The prize and the setting. Six gates deep from Sol — the end of a long, cuttable supply line. Gate anchors at the gas giant Jefferson; Sonora the living world lies sunward. The whole SIGINT game plays out here.

61 Virginis.role: A Sun-like branch target hanging off Gliese 1154 — part of why the corridor was worth building. A near-future or parallel American colony.

Gliese 486.role: A Virgo red dwarf that lets the Commonwealth step off the shared corridor at GL Vir without an over-long jump, then sprint up to Beta Comae Berenices.

Beta Com.role: Beta Comae Berenices — the Commonwealth's stepping-stone, high in declination off the corridor. From here it's a short 8.2 ly climb to Chara and New Rhodesia.

Beta CVn.role: Chara, the most Sun-like of the colonized stars — the Commonwealth's African-preserve world. Reached only through the shared corridor, so it depends on those gates staying open.

Barnard's Star.role: The French tree's first stepping-stone — the second-closest star to Sol. France launches its own relay from here toward Draco, independent of the capitalist corridor.

Struve 2398.role: A red-dwarf binary high in Draco — the French waypoint that bends the chain north toward their prize at Sigma Draconis.

Sigma Draconis.role: Alsafi — the French colony Vespera: a hot, dark-jungle hothouse world (0.8 g, 30-hour day) where colonists live indoors and France runs its premier bioengineering and physics research.

Epsilon Eridani.role: Japan's forward waystation — a nearby orange dwarf with a famous debris disk. The industrial #2 power runs its own short tree from Sol out toward Cetus.

Tau Ceti.role: The classic Sun-like target — Japan's flagship colony, a clean G8 dwarf reached via Epsilon Eridani. The capitalist coalition's second great holding after Sonora.

Sirius.role: China's target since the start of the race. A blazing A-type primary with a white-dwarf companion — no habitable world of its own, but a prestige anchor and a forward base aimed squarely at the capitalist sphere.
